test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2023: Official Paper (Held On: 03 Aug, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A train starts from a station P for another station Q at 6 p.m. at an average speed of 75 km per hour. Another train starts from station Q for station P at 8 p.m. at an average speed of 105 km per hour. If the distance between these two stations is 690 km, then at what time will the two trains meet?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance covered by the first train in 2 hours = 75 × 2 = 150 km.

Remaining distance at 8 p.m. = 690 − 150 = 540 km.

Relative speed (opposite direction) = 75 + 105 = 180 km/h.

Time to meet = 540 ÷ 180 = 3 hours.

Meeting time = 8:00 p.m. + 3 hours = 11:00 p.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 p.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance between stations P and Q = 690 km

Speed of the train starting from P at 6 p.m. = 75 km/h

Speed of the train starting from Q at 8 p.m. = 105 km/h

**Calculations:**

⇒ The first train travels alone for 2 hours (from 6 p.m. to 8 p.m.).

⇒ Distance covered by the first train = 75 × 2 = 150 km.

⇒ Remaining distance between the two trains at 8 p.m. = 690 − 150 = 540 km.

⇒ From 8 p.m. onwards, both trains move towards each other.

⇒ Relative speed = Speed of train P + Speed of train Q = 75 + 105 = 180 km/h.

⇒ Time taken to cover the remaining distance = Distance ÷ Relative speed

⇒ Time taken = 540 ÷ 180 = 3 hours.

⇒ The two trains will meet 3 hours after 8 p.m.

⇒ Meeting time = 8:00 p.m. + 3 hours = 11:00 p.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 p.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects travel towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects travel in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their speeds (|S₁ − S₂|).

Meeting Time Formula

Meeting Time = Total Initial Distance between them ÷ Relative Speed.
